The program counts arithmetic progressions. It builds a set of pairs (i, j-i) for all 0≤i≤j≤79, then for each pair with t=j-i>0, it counts how many sub-APs exist starting at i with step t.

For a pair (s, t) with t>0, the AP has elements s, s+t, s+2t, ... up to ≤79. The dp in `f()` produces dp[q]=1 for q=0 to L where L=floor((79-s)/t)+1, adding 1 to ans[0] through ans[L].

So for k≥2: ans[k] = sum over all (i,t) pairs with t>0 of [floor((79-i)/t) ≥ k-1] = sum_{m=0}^{79} floor(m/(k-1))
